Method and scope

How this was done

Full crawl of the www property across the US, CA and UK storefronts. Covers indexation, crawl efficiency, structured data, internationalisation, page experience and internal linking. Excludes the help centre subdomain, the careers site and paid landing pages under /lp/, which are noindexed by design and out of contract for this engagement.

What it was built from
SourceWindowConfidence
Screaming Frog SEO Spider 21.42026-08-11 to 2026-08-13high
Google Search Console, Pages and Performance reports2026-05-15 to 2026-08-12high
Server access logs, Cloudflare Logpush2026-07-14 to 2026-08-13high
PageSpeed Insights field data, CrUX28 day rolling to 2026-08-12medium
Ahrefs Site Explorer2026-08-12 snapshotmedium
Manual review, Chrome 141 and Googlebot smartphone UA2026-08-13 to 2026-08-18high
What it could not see

Log coverage starts 14 July, so anything before that is inferred from Search Console rather than observed at the server. The Shopify checkout flow could not be crawled with an authenticated session, so cart and checkout templates were reviewed manually on three sample journeys rather than at scale. CrUX field data is unavailable for the CA storefront because it sits below the reporting threshold, so mobile page experience for Canada is estimated from lab data only. No access to the CMS staging environment was granted, so effort estimates for template level fixes are the consultant's judgement rather than a developer's.

How priority is worked out

Every finding is scored the same way, so two written weeks apart stay comparable. Effort sits under a square root deliberately: dividing by it outright would make the register recommend nothing but trivia.

score = 3 × (severity × reach × confidence × leverage) ÷ sqrt(effort) × risk factor, capped at 100

P1 CRWL-001

Faceted navigation exposes 41,286 crawlable parameter URLs that duplicate 214 category pages

What we found

Measured from 30 days of Cloudflare Logpush records filtered to verified Googlebot by reverse DNS. 1,412,880 Googlebot requests total, 542,545 of which resolved to URLs carrying a filter parameter.

The evidence
Unique URLs returning 200 under /collections/ with one or more filter parameters41,2862026-08-13
Distinct rendered title tags across those URLs2142026-08-13
Googlebot requests to filtered URLs as a share of all crawl requests, 30 day log window38.4 percent2026-08-13
Filtered URLs carrying a self referencing canonical41,286 of 41,2862026-08-13
1 The facet component renders every filter state as a crawlable anchor, so each combination becomes a URL Googlebot can reach. 2026-08-13
90
P1 / Do this first
URLs affected
41286
Effort
0.5 dev days
Owner
Platform engineering, with SEO reviewing the link component change
Verify by
2026-10-15
The fix
  1. Add a robots.txt disallow for /collections/*?*filter= and the four other parameter prefixes listed in the appendix
  2. Strip filter parameters from every internal link in the facet component so no crawlable path into the space remains
  3. Return the parameter URLs as noindex,follow for 60 days before the disallow lands, so already indexed variants can drop out
  4. Set the Shopify theme to render facet state client side after the first interaction rather than as a link href
  5. Re-pull the log sample 30 days after deploy and confirm the filtered share of crawl is below 5 percent

Paginated category pages canonicalise to page one, removing 8,940 products from the index

What we found

Count of distinct product URLs whose only internal link path runs through a paginated category page at ?page=2 or deeper, taken from the Screaming Frog inlink report. Verified by removing category paths from the link graph and re-running the orphan report.

The fix
  1. Change the canonical on ?page=2 and deeper to reference the paginated URL itself
  2. Keep the noindex off those pages, they should be indexable and thin, not absent
  3. Publish an HTML sitemap of every product grouped by category, linked from the footer
  4. Confirm the XML sitemap lists all 4,213 products, it currently lists 3,006

The fix

P4 PERF-001

Mobile category pages report a 75th percentile LCP of 4.8 seconds, driven by an unsized hero image

What we found

CrUX 28 day rolling field data for the origin, filtered to the /collections/ URL group and mobile form factor, pulled 12 August. Only 31 percent of visits meet the good threshold of 2.5 seconds.

The evidence

1 The hero banner is the LCP element on every category page. It carries no width or height and is lazy loaded despite sitting above the fold. 2026-08-17

The fix
  1. Remove loading=lazy from the hero image, it is always above the fold
  2. Add width and height attributes so the layout does not shift while it loads
  3. Add a srcset with 640, 960 and 1440 wide sources and a sizes attribute matching the template
  4. Add fetchpriority=high to the hero img
  5. Re-measure in the lab, then wait 28 days for the field data to move
